verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's own pages tout a second-gen FP8 Transformer Engine for 'LLM prototyping, inference, and AI development across frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch' (docs-21) and generic agentic-AI/fine-tuning claims (docs-1, docs-23), but none of the evidence names FP4 support or any of the specific serving stacks in the story (TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, ROCm, llama.cpp). A hands-on community report directly complicates the story, noting the card's SM120 architecture 'lack[s] support in main libraries' because ecosystem focus has shifted to B300/SM100 (comm-4), even though another user reports functioning multi-GPU inference at 41k tok/s (comm-1) — a real but partial and contested picture rather than a clean documented story. Missing for 10: explicit FP4 documentation, named integration with TensorRT-LLM/vLLM/llama.cpp, and resolution of the SM120 library-support gap flagged by the community.
